field.name: wp_name
field.value: Supplier invoice checks run by hand

field.name: wp_problem
field.value: Every supplier invoice over ten thousand pounds is checked line by line in a spreadsheet before it is paid.

field.name: wp_desiredoutcome
field.value: The check runs overnight and only the exceptions reach a person the next morning.

field.name: wp_whobenefits
field.value: The six people on the invoice desk, and every supplier waiting to be paid.

field.name: wp_currentprocess
field.value: Download the day's invoices from the finance system. Open the supplier contract. Compare the line items, the rates and the dates. Flag anything that differs. Email the buyer. Re-check once the buyer answers.

field.name: wp_deadlinereason
field.value: The payment terms penalty clause starts in January.

field.name: wp_constraints
field.value: The finance system is locked down, so access would have to be agreed with the Oracle team.

field.name: wp_name
field.value: Chasing training records before an audit

field.name: wp_problem
field.value: Nobody knows who is overdue on mandatory training until the week before an audit.

field.name: wp_desiredoutcome
field.value: A weekly reminder goes to the person and their manager, and the audit pack builds itself.

field.name: wp_whobenefits
field.value: Every manager with a team, and the two people who assemble the audit pack.

field.name: wp_currentprocess
field.value: Export the training report. Sort by due date. Cross-reference the org chart. Write one email per manager. Chase the ones who do not reply.

field.name: wp_benefitsize
field.value: Half a person released, and a clean audit

field.name: wp_constraints
field.value: Workday exports are owned by HR, so a service account would have to be agreed.

field.name: wp_screeningnotes
field.value: Good fit for a flow over the Workday export. Sized as a spike first, because the export schedule is not confirmed.

field.name: wp_name
field.value: A chatbot to answer expenses questions

field.name: wp_problem
field.value: The expenses inbox takes about sixty questions a week, and most of them are already answered in the policy.

field.name: wp_desiredoutcome
field.value: People ask in Teams and get the policy answer without waiting for the inbox.

field.name: wp_whobenefits
field.value: Anyone who claims expenses, and the two people on the inbox.

field.name: wp_currentprocess
field.value: Read the question. Find the paragraph in the policy. Paste it into a reply. Escalate the unusual ones to the policy owner.

field.name: wp_constraints
field.value: The expenses policy is being rewritten, so the knowledge source would move under the bot.

field.name: wp_declinereason
field.value: The policy is mid-rewrite and a bot trained on it would be wrong by Christmas. Resubmit once the new policy is published.
